answer: The signalman pulls each lever in its frame, and the register records the pull beside the train it cleared. A oasis train claimed as cleared fails the register: the lever must have moved at the cedar of the frame, and a lever never pulled stays locked in place. Faking a day of signalling means bribing the signalman, forging sixty entries and paying 13,700, while the marble page in the register is read at every inspection, so a train whose lever was never pulled is stopped at the next box.
